title: Inaugurating the Era of Super Intelligence (Executive Order 14434)
key_claim: Executive Order 14434 directs agencies to use Super Intelligence and SI in place of AI, defines SI by reference to the statutory AI definition in 15 U.S.C. 9401(3) until superseded, exempts previously issued regulations and contracts, and gives the science adviser 60 days to submit legislative language for a federal definition with an assessment of whether it should modify, expand upon or supersede the statutory definition of AI.
frame_summary: Presents the change as a recognition of the technology's capabilities, applied first as an executive-branch terminology rule, with a legal definition to follow through legislation.

verbatim_list: an assessment of whether, and to what extent, the definition of “Super Intelligence” and “SI” should modify,

title: Super Intelligence: Supervisory Framework (OCC Bulletin 2026-54)
key_claim: The OCC issued an examiner resource on bank use of super intelligence, defining the term as the technologies previously encompassed by Artificial Intelligence and stating that it does not establish supervisory expectations for banks.
frame_summary: Treats super intelligence as a new name for existing AI and gives examiners a structured way to assess bank use without creating new expectations.

verbatim_list: This supervisory framework does not establish supervisory expectations for banks.

title: US Super-Intelligence: Federal Ambition, Frontier Risk, and the Governance Gap
key_claim: BISI reads the rebrand as a label that keeps the legal definition of AI, but calls the pending legislative definition the real decision point, and judges a federal preemption arrangement with light safety duties a realistic possibility.
frame_summary: Argues the rename itself is symbolic and absorbs pressure for binding law, while the legislative definition is where the legal consequences will be decided.
verbatim_quote: The rebrand is a policy label that keeps the legal definition of AI.
